reasoning:
A 4x4 0/1 matrix with all row and column sums 2 and zero diagonal is a 2-regular simple bipartite graph on 4+4 labeled vertices with the four diagonal edges i-i forbidden. A 2-regular bipartite graph is a disjoint union of even cycles of length >= 4, so on 8 vertices it is either two 4-cycles or one 8-cycle.

Case 1 - two disjoint 4-cycles: a 4-cycle on row pair R and column pair C uses all four edges R x C, so it contains a diagonal edge iff R intersect C is nonempty. Zero diagonal forces each column pair to be the complement of its row pair, i.e. the column partition equals the row partition with pairs matched to complements. Unordered pair partitions of {1,2,3,4}: 3. Subtotal 3.

Case 2 - one 8-cycle: represent a cycle by cyclic row order p (4!/4/2 = 3 distinct orders) and column sequence q=(q1..q4), edges (p_i,q_i) and (p_{i+1},q_i), indices mod 4. Zero diagonal means q_i not in {p_i, p_{i+1}}. For p=(1,2,3,4): q1 in {3,4}, q2 in {1,4}, q3 in {1,2}, q4 in {2,3}. Enumerating: q1=3 forces q4=2,q3=1,q2=4 giving (3,4,1,2); q1=4 forces q2=1,q3=2,q4=3 giving (4,1,2,3). So 2 valid q per row order. Subtotal 3 x 2 = 6.

Total: 3 + 6 = 9.
